questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A solid sphere of radius $R$ has moment of inertia / about its diameter. What will be moment of inertia of a shell of same mass and same radius about its diameter ?
questions.solution:
For a solid sphere, $I=\frac{2}{5} M R^2$
For a spherical shell, $\begin{aligned} I^{\prime} & =\frac{2}{3} M R^2 \\ & =\frac{5}{3} \times \frac{2}{5} M R^2=\frac{5}{3} I\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A solid sphere of mass 2 kg rolls on a smooth horizontal surface at $10 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}$ and then rolls up a smooth $30^{\circ}$ incline. The maximum height reached by the sphere is $\left(g=9.8 \mathrm{~m} / \mathrm{s}^2\right)$
questions.solution:
Applying conservation of mechanical energy, we can write
$\frac{1}{2} I \omega^2+\frac{1}{2} m v^2=m g h$ where, $h$ is maximum height reached by the sphere, $v$ is linear velocity and $\omega$ is angular velocity of the sphere. $\frac{1}{2} I\left(\frac{v}{r}\right)^2+\frac{1}{2} m v^2=m g h \quad[\because v=\omega r]\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \frac{1}{2} \times \frac{2}{5} m r^2 \times \frac{v^2}{r^2}+\frac{1}{2} m v^2=m g h \\ & \frac{1}{5} m v^2+\frac{1}{2} m v^2=m g h \\ & \frac{7}{10} m v^2=m g h \\ & h=\frac{7}{10} \times \frac{v^2}{g}=\frac{7}{10} \times \frac{10^2}{9.8}=\frac{70}{9.8} \\ &=\frac{100}{14}=\frac{50}{7}=7.1 \mathrm{~m}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A uniform thin bar of mass 6 m and length $12 L$ is bent to make a regular hexagon. Its moment of inertia about an axis passing through the centre of mass and perpendicular to the plane of hexagon is :
questions.solution:
Length of each side of hexagon $=2 L$ and mass of each side $=m$
Let $O$ be the centre of mass of hexagon. Therefore, perpendicular distance of $O$ from each side, $r=L \tan 60^{\circ}=L \sqrt{3}$ The desired moment of inertia of hexagon about $O$ is $\begin{aligned} I & =6\left[I_{\text {one side }}\right]=6\left[\frac{m(2 L)^2}{12}+m r^2\right] \\ & =6\left[\frac{mL^2}{3}+m(L \sqrt{3})^2\right] \\ & =20 mL^2\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Four thin rods of same mass $M$ and same length $l$, form a square as shown in figure Moment of inertia of this system about an axis through centre $O$ and perpendicular to its plane is
questions.solution:
Moment of inertia of rod $A B$ about point $P=\frac{1}{12} M I^2$
Ml of rod $A B$ about point $O=\frac{M l^2}{12}+M\left(\frac{I}{2}\right)^2=\frac{1}{3} M l^2$ [from the theorem of parallel axis] and the system consists of 4 rods of similar type so by the symmetry $I_{\text {system }}=\frac{4}{3} M l^2$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A disc of mass 5 kg and radius 50 cm rolls on the ground at the rate of $10 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$. Find the kinetic energy of the disc in J .
questions.solution:
Here, mass of the disc, $M=5 \mathrm{~kg}$
Radius of the disc, $R=50 \mathrm{~cm}=1 / 2 \mathrm{~m}$ Linear velocity of the disc, $v=10 \mathrm{~ms}^{-1}$ 
As,  $\quad v=R \omega\therefore \quad 10=\frac{1}{2} \omega$ or $\omega=10 \times 2=20 \mathrm{rad} \mathrm{s}^{-1}$
Also, moment of inertia of disc about an axis through its centre,
$I=\frac{1}{2} M R^2=\frac{1}{2} \times 5 \times\left(\frac{1}{2}\right)^2=\frac{5}{8} \mathrm{~kg}^2-\mathrm{m}\begin{aligned} & \therefore \mathrm{KE} \text { of translation }=\frac{1}{2} m v^2=\frac{1}{2} \times 5 \times(10)^2=250 \mathrm{~J} \\ & \text { Rotational kinetic energy }=\frac{1}{2} / \omega^2=\frac{1}{2}\left(\frac{5}{8}\right)(20)^2=125 \mathrm{~J}\end{aligned}\begin{aligned} \text { Total kinetic energy } & =\text { Translational }+ \text { Rotational } \\ & =(250+125)=375 \mathrm{~J}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A solid cylinder is rolling down on an inclined plane of angle $\theta$. The coefficient of static friction between the plane and the cylinder is $\mu_s$. The condition for the cylinder not to slip is
questions.solution:
$\because$ Linear acceleration for rolling, $a=\frac{g \sin \ddot{\theta}}{\sqrt{1+k^2 / R^2}}$
For cylinder, $\frac{k^2}{R^2}=\frac{1}{2}\therefore \quad a_{\text {cylinder }}=\frac{2}{3} g \sin \theta$ For rotation, the torque $F R=I \alpha \cdot\left(M R^2 \alpha\right) / 2$ (where, $F=$ force of friction) But $\quad R \alpha=a \quad \therefore \quad F=\frac{M}{2} aF=\frac{M}{2} \cdot \frac{2}{3} g \sin \theta=\frac{M}{3} g \sin \theta\therefore \quad \mu_s=\frac{F}{N}$, where $N$ is normal reaction, $\mu_s=\frac{\frac{M}{3} g \sin \theta}{M g \cos \theta}=\frac{\tan \theta}{3}\therefore$ For rolling without slipping of a roller down, the inclined plane, $\tan \theta \leq 3 \mu_s$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A particle of mass $m$ is projected with a velocity $v$ at an angle of $45^{\circ}$ with horizontal. When the particle is at its maximum height, the magnitude of its angular momentum about the point of projection is :
questions.solution:
Maximum height
$H=\frac{v^2 \sin ^2 45^{\circ}}{2 g}=\frac{v^2}{2 g} \times \frac{1}{2}=\frac{v^2}{4 g}$
Momentum of particle at the highest point
$p=m v \cos 45^{\circ}=m v / \sqrt{2}$
Angular momentum $=\mathrm{pH}=\frac{m v}{\sqrt{2}} \times \frac{v^2}{4 g}=\frac{m v^3}{4 \sqrt{2} g}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A wheel is rotating with an angular speed of $20 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}$. It is stopped to rest by applying a constant torque in 4 s . If the moment of inertia of the wheel about its axis is $0.20 \mathrm{~kg} / \mathrm{m}^2$, then the work done by the torque in two seconds will be
questions.solution:
$\omega_1=20 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}, \quad \omega=0, \quad t=4 \mathrm{~s} . \quad$ So angular retardation $\alpha=\frac{\omega_1-\omega_2}{t}=\frac{20}{4}=5 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}^2$
Now, angular speed after 2s $\omega_2=\omega_1-\alpha t=20-5 \times 2=10 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}$
Work done by torque in $2 \mathrm{~s}=$ loss in kinetic
$\begin{aligned}
\text { energy } & =\frac{1}{2} /\left(\omega_1{ }^2-\omega_1^2\right)=\frac{1}{2}(0.20)\left((20)^2-(10)^2\right) \\
& =\frac{1}{2}(0.20)(400-100) \\
& =\frac{1}{2}(0.20) \times(300)=\frac{1}{2} \times 60=30
\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A solid sphere of mass $M$, radius $R$ and having moment of inertia about an axis passing through the centre of mass as $I$, is recast into a disc of thickness $t$, whose moment of inertia about an axis passing through its edge and perpendicular to its plane remains $I$. Then, radius of the disc will be
questions.solution: $\begin{aligned} \frac{2}{5} M R^2 & =\frac{3}{2} M r^2 \\ r & =\frac{2 R}{\sqrt{15}}\end{aligned}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The moment of inertia of a body about a given axis is $1.2 \mathrm{~kg}-\mathrm{m}^2$. To produce a rotational kinetic energy of 1500 J an angular acceleration of $25 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}^2$ must be applied for
questions.solution:
Kinetic energy of rotation is half the product of the moment of inertia $(l)$ of the body and the square of the angular velocity $(\omega)$ of the body.
Kinetic energy of rotation $=\frac{1}{2} \times$ moment of inertia × angular velocity
i.e., $\quad K=\frac{1}{2} / \omega^2\omega^2=\frac{2 K}{1}$
Given $l=1.2 \mathrm{~kg} \mathrm{~m}^2, K=1500 \mathrm{~J}\omega^2=\frac{2 \times 1500}{1.2}\Rightarrow \quad \omega=50 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}$
From the equation of angular motion, we have
$\omega=\omega_0+\alpha t$
where $\omega_0$ is initial angular velocity, $\alpha$ is angular acceleration and $t$ is time
given $\omega_0=0\begin{aligned} & \omega=50 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s} \\ & \alpha=25 \mathrm{rad} / \mathrm{s}^2 \\ & t=\frac{\omega}{\alpha}=\frac{50}{25}=2 \mathrm{~s}\end{aligned}$

questions.q: A circular disc of radius $\frac{R}{3}$ is cut from a circular disc of radius $R$ and mass $9 M$ as shown. Then, moment of inertia of remaining disc about ' $O$ ' perpendicular to the plane of the disc is
questions.solution: $I_0=\frac{9 M R^2}{2}-\left[\frac{M(R / 3)^2}{2}+M\left(\frac{2 R}{3}\right)^2\right]=4 M R^2$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: The moment of inertia of a disc of mass $m$ and radius $R$ about an axis, which is tangential to the circumference of the disc and parallel to its diameter is
questions.solution:
Use parallel axis theorem, from the theorem of parallel axis, the moment of inertia ( $/$ ) of a body about given axis is equal to its moment of inertia/about its diameter, plus the product of the mass $M$ of the body and square of perpendicular distanće between the two axes. That is
$I=I_d+M R^2=\frac{1}{4} M R^2+M R^2=\frac{5}{4} M R^2$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Angular momentum is conserved
questions.solution: According to law of conservation of angular momentum if there is no torque on the system, then the angular momentum remains constant.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A circular disc is rotating with angular velocity $\omega$. If a man standing at the edge of the disc walks towards its centre then the angular velocity of the disc will
questions.solution:
When no external force acts on a body its angular moment remains conserved.
From law of conservation of angular momentum, we have
$J=l \omega=$ constant
where $/$ is moment of inertia of the body and $\omega$ is angular velocity.
Also $I=\frac{1}{2} M R^2$ (for disc) where $M$ is mass and $R$ is radius of disc.
$J=\frac{1}{2} M R^2 \omega=$ constant
Since, man moves towards the centre of the disc, distance of mass distribution $R$ decreases hence, $\omega$ increases.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two spheres of equal masses, one of which is $a$ thin spherical shell and the other a solid, have the same moment of inertia about their respective diameters. The ratio of their radii will be
questions.solution:
Let the radii of the thin spherical and the solid sphere are $R_1$ and $R_2$ respectively.
Then the moment of inertia of the spherical shell about their diameter
$I=\frac{2}{3} M R_1^2$  ....(i)
and the moment of inertia of the solid sphere is given by
$I=\frac{2}{5} M R_2^2$  ....(ii)
Given that the masses and moment of inertia for both the bodies are equal, then from Eqs. (i) and (ii)
$\frac{2}{3} M R_1^2=\frac{2}{5} M R_2^2 \Rightarrow \frac{R_1^2}{R_2^2}=\frac{3}{5}\Rightarrow \quad \frac{R}{R_2}=\sqrt{\frac{3}{5}} \Rightarrow R_1: R_2=\sqrt{3}: \sqrt{5}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: If the angular momentum of any rotating body increases by 200 %, then the increase in its kinetic energy is
questions.solution:
$\begin{aligned} E & =\frac{L^2}{2 l} \\ E & \propto L^2 \\ \frac{E_2}{E_1} & =\left(\frac{L_2}{L_1}\right)^2 \\ \frac{E_2}{E_1} & =\left[\frac{L_1+200 \% \text { of } L_1}{L_1}\right] \\ & =\left[\frac{L_1+2 L_1}{L_1}\right]^2=(3)^2 \\ E_2 & =9 E_1 \end{aligned}$
Increment in kinetic energy $\begin{aligned} \Delta E & =E_2-E_1 \\ & =9 E_1-E_1 \\ \Delta E & =8 E_1 \\ \frac{\Delta E}{E_1} & =8 \end{aligned}$ or percentage increase $=800 \%$

questions.solution: $L=m v r=m \sqrt{\frac{G M}{r}} r=m \sqrt{G M r}\therefore \quad L \propto \sqrt{r}\begin{array}{rlrl}\Rightarrow  \frac{L_2}{L_1}  =\sqrt{\frac{r_2}{r_1}} \\  =\sqrt{\frac{16 r}{r}}=4 \\ \Rightarrow \quad  L_2  =4 L\end{array}$

questions.q: A constant torque acting on a uniform circular wheel changes its angular momentum from $A_0$ to $4 A_0$ in 4 s . The magnitude of this torque is
questions.solution: Torque $\vec{\tau}=\frac{\overrightarrow{\mathrm{dL}}}{d t}=\frac{L_2-L_1}{\Delta t}=\frac{4 A_0-A_0}{4}=\frac{3 A_0}{4}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: A small object of uniform density rolls up a curved surface with an initial velocity $v$. It reaches upto a maximum height of $\frac{7 v^2}{10 g}$ with respect to initial position. Then the object is
questions.solution:
By the conservation of energy, $\begin{aligned} & & E_i & =E_f \\ \Rightarrow & & \frac{1}{2} m v^2+\frac{1}{2} l \omega^2 & =m g H=m g\left(\frac{7 v^2}{10 g}\right) \\ \Rightarrow & & \frac{1}{2} m v^2+\frac{1}{2} l \cdot \frac{v^2}{R^2} & =\frac{7}{10} m v^2 \quad(\because v=\omega R) \\ \Rightarrow & & \frac{1}{2} I \cdot \frac{v^2}{R^2} & =\left(\frac{7}{10}-\frac{1}{2}\right) m v^2 \\ & & & =\frac{2}{10} m v^2=\frac{1}{5} m v^2 \\ \therefore & & I & =\frac{2}{5} m R^2 \end{aligned}$
The above value of moment of inertia is equal to moment of inertia of solid sphere.

questions.q: A uniform rod of length 2 m , specific gravity 0.5 and mass 2 kg is hinged at one end to the bottom of a tank of water (specific gravity $=1.0$ ) filled upto a height of 1 m as shown in the figure. Taking the case $\theta \neq 0^{\circ}$, the force exerted by the hinge on the rod is
questions.solution:
Length of rod inside the water $=1 \sec \theta=\sec \theta$
Upthrust, $\quad F=\left(\frac{2}{2}\right)(\sec \theta)\left(\frac{1}{500}\right)(1000)(10)\begin{aligned} & \Rightarrow \quad F=20 \sec \theta \\ & \text { Weight of rod, } w=20 \times 10=20 \mathrm{~N}\end{aligned}$ For rotational equilibrium of rod, net torque about O should be zero. $\therefore F\left(\frac{\sec \theta}{2}\right)(\sin \theta)=w=(1 \sin \theta)\Rightarrow \quad \frac{20}{2} \sec ^2 \theta=20\begin{array}{ll}\Rightarrow & \theta=45^{\circ} \\ \Rightarrow & F=20 \sec 45^{\circ}\end{array}F=20 \sqrt{2} \mathrm{~N}$ For vertical equilibrium of rod, force exerted by the hinge on the rod will be $(20 \sqrt{2}-20) \mathrm{N}$ downwards i.e. 8.3 N downwards

questions.q:
A rod of length $L$ is composed of a uniform length $\frac{L}{2}$ of wood whose mass in $m_w$ and a uniform length $\frac{L}{2}$ of brass whose mass is $m_b$.
The moment of inertia / of the rod about an axis perpendicular to the rod and through its centre is equal to
questions.solution:
For a thin uniform rod, moment of inertia about an axis through its centre perpendicular to length
of rod, $I=\frac{1}{12} M L^2$
Here, $\quad M=\left(m_w+m_b\right)\therefore A \quad I=\frac{1}{12}\left(m_w+m_b\right) L^2$
